semantic_adjudication.basis: NL4 derived contract (NL-CONTRACT-NL4-DERIVED-bb8ee858f534509576fa), source PlantUML line 5 with <<submachine>> stereotype, source body lines 6-7 showing no nested states, FCSTM state:Autonomous:line:9 as a leaf with children=0, and the flat sibling structure of AutonomousIdle/AutonomousActive/AutonomousFinal.
semantic_adjudication.reason: The source PlantUML annotates Autonomous with the <<submachine>> stereotype (line 5) but the state body (lines 6-7) contains no nested child states. AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, and AutonomousFinal are declared at the top level as siblings. In PlantUML, the <<submachine>> stereotype is a presentation annotation; actual containment requires states to be nested inside the submachine's block. The FCSTM correctly reflects the source's actual flat structure (children=0, is_composite=false). The NL requires autonomous mode to have sub-states (composite structure). The source's incomplete specification—labeling something as a submachine without providing sub-states—results in a model that cannot satisfy the containment obligation. The rebuttal that 'the closed model is consistent with itself' is not competent: consistency with the source's flat structure does not satisfy the NL's composite requirement. The divergence is precisely the issue: the author's indicated intent (submachine) is not realized in the source's actual structure.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: Autonomous must be a composite with the sub-states the requirement assigns to it; the source declares <<submachine>> but provides no actual child states.

result.reason: The behavior_consequence lens identifies four violated obligations by comparing NL-derived contracts against the closed FCSTM's deterministic facts. (1) Autonomous is declared simple rather than composite, violating the submachine requirement. (2) Because Autonomous is not composite, it contains no sub-states, violating the containment obligation. (3) No transition exists from Autonomous to HumanDriving in the complete inventory; the closest transitions originate from AutonomousActive, a sibling state. (4) The Power_Off event is only consumable from HumanDriving; the reachable operating states Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, and AutonomousActive have no Power_Off transitions, so the system cannot always reach the final state. Contracts REF-001, REF-004, REF-005, REF-007, and REF-008 are satisfied by the observed model facts and are omitted from this sparse response.

decisions.basis: NL2 contract (NL-CONTRACT-NL2-DECL-1), FCSTM state:Autonomous:line:9 with is_composite=false, inspection metrics composite_state_count=1, source PlantUML line 5 with <<submachine>> stereotype, and the closed-model state inventory showing Autonomous as a non-composite leaf.
decisions.reason: The NL explicitly requires Autonomous to be a submachine (composite) state. The FCSTM inspection facts confirm state:Autonomous:line:9 has is_composite=false, and composite_state_count=1 (only the root wrapper). The PlantUML source annotates Autonomous with <<submachine>> but the FCSTM lowering flattened it to a simple state. The strongest alternative reading—that FCSTM may represent composites differently—is not supported by any exact fact; the inspection metrics and state inventory definitively show no composite declaration for Autonomous. The structural form required by the NL is absent in the closed model.
decisions.violated_obligation: Autonomous mode must be declared as a composite (submachine) state capable of containing sub-states, per NL2 'The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state.'

decisions.basis: NL2 contract (NL-CONTRACT-NL2-CONTAIN-1), complete FCSTM state inventory showing parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010 for all leaf states, and source references to AutonomousIdle and AutonomousActive as conceptually sub-states in the author's diagram but flat siblings in the model.
decisions.reason: The NL requires containment of sub-states within Autonomous. The complete FCSTM state inventory shows all five leaf states (HumanDriving, Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, AutonomousFinal) are direct children of the root wrapper with parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010; zero states have parent=Autonomous. The strongest alternative—that transitions from Autonomous to AutonomousIdle represent sub-state behavior—is not competent: transitions are behavioral links between siblings in a flat hierarchy, not structural containment. The NL's 'has sub-states' is a structural property requiring parent-child relations, which are entirely absent.
decisions.violated_obligation: Autonomous mode must contain at least one sub-state (child state) in the closed model, per NL2 'The autonomous mode has sub-states.'

decisions.basis: NL4.2 contract (NL-CONTRACT-NL4.2-ENDPOINT-1), S2 predicate receipt with verdict=false, complete FCSTM transition inventory (8 transitions), source transitions tr_0005/tr_0006 showing source=AutonomousActive, and the exact endpoint binding source=Autonomous target=HumanDriving.

decisions.basis: NL4 derived contract (NL-CONTRACT-NL4-DERIVED-7ecf0629a5bf1dc21604), S5 predicate receipt with verdict=false (observed guard=null vs expected 'front_distance > 10'), FCSTM transition:line:19 with triggers=[Front_Distance_10_2] and guard=null, and event:Front_Distance_10_2:line:4 encoding the same condition as a trigger.

The NL states 'when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state' which is the first violated-obligation reading (requiring a guard). This constitutes a surviving undercutting ambiguity between two competent semantic encodings.

issues.expected: Autonomous mode contains at least one sub-state as a child, establishing a hierarchical containment relation.
issues.observed: Autonomous is not composite and therefore has no children. AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive, and AutonomousFinal are all siblings under the root wrapper (parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0010), not descendants of Autonomous.
issues.reason: The NL requires Autonomous to contain sub-states. Because the FCSTM does not declare Autonomous as composite, no containment relation exists. No frozen predicate covers the containment property, so this remains a precisely bound W1 candidate with exact state refs.
issues.requirement_quote: The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source inventory shows a transition from Autonomous to AutonomousIdle (tr_0003), which in a composite model would indicate containment; the behavioral sequence Autonomous → AutonomousIdle → AutonomousActive is preserved, so the operational flow is intact despite the missing structural nesting.
issues.title: Autonomous mode contains no sub-states in the closed model

issues.basis: NL5 with system-level scope; derived contract REF-009; inspection event_consumer facts for Power_Off showing consumer_state_refs=[HumanDriving] only; reachability facts confirming Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, AutonomousActive are all reachable_from_initial=true; FCSTM transition inventory confirming no Power_Off edge from those three states.
issues.expected: The Power Off event must be accepted (consumed) from all operating states of the system so that the system can always transition to the final state regardless of its current active state.
issues.observed: The deterministic event_consumer fact shows Power_Off is consumed only by transition:line:20 (source=HumanDriving, target=AutonomousFinal). The reachable operating states Autonomous, AutonomousIdle, and AutonomousActive have no outgoing transition triggered by Power_Off. If the system is in any of these three states when Power_Off occurs, no transition fires and the system cannot reach the final state.
issues.reason: The derived event_consumer_coverage contract requires Power_Off to be consumable from all operating states. Deterministic facts show exactly one consumer (HumanDriving via transition:line:20) while three other reachable operating states lack any Power_Off transition. No frozen predicate covers system-wide event consumer coverage, so this remains a precisely bound W1 candidate.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL segment NL5 states 'when power off, it will transit to final state' without explicitly enumerating all source states; one could argue the obligation is only that the transition exists from the state the system is in at the moment of power off, and the author intended only HumanDriving as the relevant state. However, the derived contract (REF-009) explicitly extends the obligation to all operating states based on the system-level scope, and the behavioral consequence of being unable to power off from AutonomousIdle or AutonomousActive is a clear operational gap.
issues.title: Power Off event not consumable from all reachable operating states
